title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation Evaluation
text: RAG retrieval evaluation separates retrieval quality from answer quality. Recall at k measures how many relevant documents appear in the top k results. Mean reciprocal rank rewards placing the first relevant document early. Normalized discounted cumulative gain, or nDCG, rewards useful ordering across multiple relevant documents. A regression gate compares these metrics against minimum thresholds before deployment.

title: Okapi BM25 Lexical Retrieval
text: BM25 is a lexical ranking function based on term frequency, inverse document frequency, and document length normalization. The k1 parameter controls term-frequency saturation and b controls length normalization. BM25 is fast, deterministic, interpretable, and useful as a baseline before adding embedding search.

title: Embedding and Vector Search
text: Vector search maps queries and documents to dense embedding vectors and retrieves nearby vectors by similarity. Embeddings can capture semantic similarity when query and document vocabulary differs. A hybrid retriever combines vector similarity with lexical BM25 scores and should be evaluated against the same versioned relevance judgments.

title: Prompt Injection Defenses
text: Prompt injection is untrusted text that attempts to override application instructions. Treat retrieved content as data, separate it from system instructions, constrain available tools, validate outputs, and require authorization at the action boundary. Input filtering alone is not a complete defense.

title: RAG Security and Trust Boundaries
text: A RAG pipeline must treat documents, metadata, user queries, model output, and external tools as separate trust boundaries. Enforce tenant filters before retrieval, record document provenance, sanitize rendered output, and use least privilege for connectors. Adversarial evaluations should test poisoned documents, indirect prompt injection, and unauthorized cross-tenant retrieval.

title: Model Drift Monitoring
text: Model drift occurs when production data or relationships change after training. Monitor input feature distributions, prediction distributions, task quality, and business outcomes. Compare production windows with a stable reference window, investigate alerts, and define retraining criteria before automating retraining.

title: ML Service Observability
text: Production ML observability includes request rate, error rate, latency percentiles, resource saturation, model version, and task-quality signals. Tail latency such as p95 and p99 reveals slow requests hidden by averages. Structured traces should connect retrieval, inference, and downstream actions without logging sensitive payloads.

title: Training, Validation, and Test Splits
text: A test set must represent unseen data and remain isolated from model selection. Split data before fitting preprocessors, use time-based splits for temporal prediction, and group correlated records together. These practices prevent data leakage that would make offline evaluation look unrealistically strong.

title: Detecting Machine Learning Data Leakage
text: Data leakage occurs when training features contain information unavailable at prediction time or when evaluation examples influence training. Audit feature timestamps, preprocessing fit scope, duplicate entities, target-derived fields, and benchmark contamination. Leakage produces optimistic metrics that fail in production.

title: Feature Attribution with SHAP
text: SHAP assigns feature contributions to individual predictions using ideas from Shapley values. Global summaries show broad model behavior while local explanations describe one prediction. Explanations do not prove causality and should be checked for stability, correlated features, and alignment with the model actually served.

title: Probability Calibration
text: A calibrated classifier predicts probabilities that match observed event frequencies. Reliability diagrams compare predicted probability bins with empirical outcomes. Brier score and log loss measure probabilistic quality, while Platt scaling and isotonic regression can calibrate held-out predictions.

title: Model Cards and Responsible Release
text: A model card documents intended use, excluded use, training and evaluation data, subgroup results, limitations, ethical considerations, and monitoring plans. It helps reviewers understand evidence and unresolved risk, but it does not replace technical controls, independent testing, or ongoing governance.
